question: GQ-009
subject: defusing the retention trap instead of watching it count down
the_trap: I set log_retention_days 365 -> 3 to stop the log filling the disk, then found 6 declared derivations reading that database. They re-derived only because the oldest rows had not aged out. The audit runs them on every push.

the_fix.what: a column slice of the log on the vault, holding the rows the derivations read
the_fix.ratio: 643 KB preserves what 9.43 GB was needed for — 0.007%

verified_before_switching.method: ran all five aggregate derivations against live and slice
verified_before_switching.eviction_simulation: the slice answers 45285517 with no reference to the live log at all

deliberately_left_pointing_at_the_live_l.why: it reads a pragma about the FILE, not its rows — a statement about the live database that would be meaningless against an archive
deliberately_left_pointing_at_the_live_l.so: 1 warning remains, and it is correct

my_own_check_was_wrong_again.what: after repointing all 5, the warning count stayed at 6
my_own_check_was_wrong_again.cause: the check stringified the whole derivation object, so the source_note explaining the repoint — which necessarily names the old path — kept the warning alive
my_own_check_was_wrong_again.fix: match d.source, the field, not the serialised object
my_own_check_was_wrong_again.the_pattern: THIRD time today I matched prose instead of the thing it describes: a comment satisfied the coverage gate, a comment in gate-selftest.sh triggered a false positive, and now a note kept a resolved warning alive. The field is the fact; the note is commentary.
